john.01.39|17|staying|w11|w15: μένει describes where he was staying. ἔμειναν describes their subsequent stay.
john.01.41|18|means|w16|w17: The copula ἐστιν is rendered “means” in the gloss explanation. μεθερμηνευόμενον is rendered “translated.”
john.02.7|6|water|w7|w8: This first “water” qualifies ὑδρίας, water jars. ὕδατος renders the second occurrence.
john.03.21|19|having|w19|w18: The perfect participle εἰργασμένα supplies “having been done.” ἐστιν is its finite auxiliary.
john.04.30|2|out|w1|w3: “Went out” renders ἐξῆλθον, followed by the separate preposition ἐκ.
john.04.33|12|something||w11: The English object is implicit in the infinitive φαγεῖν, “to eat.”
john.04.38|13|labored,|w10|w15: This verb renders κεκοπιάκασιν. κόπον is the later noun “labor.”
john.04.42|15|said,|w10|w4: “What you said” renders the noun λαλιάν, her speech. ἔλεγον is the preceding “they were saying.”
john.04.48|7|people||w12: “People” makes the plural “you” explicit. ἴδητε already supplies “see” and its plural subject.
john.05.8|5|up,|w5|w6: The first “up” belongs to the command Ἔγειρε. ἆρον supplies “pick up.”
john.05.19|32|Father|w30|w25: The second “the Father” makes the subject pronoun ἐκεῖνος explicit. πατέρα is the first occurrence.
john.06.1|18|Sea||w8: “That is, the Sea of Tiberias” repeats the head noun Θαλάσσης in English.
john.06.17|16|come,|w15|w18: Darkness “had come” renders ἐγεγόνει. ἐληλύθει is the later verb about Jesus.
john.06.62|1|what||w1: The English question introduces the hypothetical with “what.” The conjunction ἐάν directly supplies “if.”
john.07.17|19|whether|w17|w12: The second “whether” belongs with ἢ. πότερον introduces the first alternative.
john.08.8|3|stooped|s4|w3: κύψας means “stooped.” κάτω contributes the following “down.”
john.08.10|7|“Woman,||w10: This vocative is supplied in the DGT. γυναικός occurs in the source’s description of the addressee.
john.08.57|12|old,|w10|w8: The Greek expression “have fifty years” becomes “are fifty years old.” “Old” reflects the age construction with ἔχεις.
john.10.21|10|demon-possessed.|w9|w11: δαιμονιζομένου describes the possessed person. δαιμόνιον is the noun in the next sentence.
john.11.39|11|man|w12|w11: The substantival participle τετελευτηκότος is rendered “man who had died.” τοῦ supplies the preceding article.
john.11.44|1|man|w4|w3: The substantival participle τεθνηκώς is rendered “man who had died.” ὁ supplies the preceding article.
john.12.13|15|out,|w12|w7: “Crying out” renders ἐκραύγαζον. ἐξῆλθον gives the earlier “went out.”
john.14.19|3|longer|w1|w7: ἔτι belongs to “a little while longer.” οὐκέτι describes when the world sees Jesus “no more.”
john.19.25|15|wife||w18: The relationship “wife” is supplied from context for Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Κλωπᾶ.
john.19.33|1|when|w5|w6: “Came” and temporal “when” render ἐλθόντες in this clause. ὡς introduces the subsequent realization.
john.20.15|28|away,|w21|w30: “Carried him away” renders ἐβάστασας. ἀρῶ is the later promise “I will take.”
john.20.19|10|day|w8|w5: The second “day” is the feminine elliptical noun with μιᾷ, “the first [day].” ἡμέρᾳ supplies the first occurrence.
john.20.23|15|sins||w5: The second “sins” supplies the understood object of “retain.” ἁμαρτίας occurs only in the first clause.
john.21.4|1|when|w4|w1: The temporal “when” reflects the genitive absolute with γενομένης. Πρωΐας is “morning.”
john.21.6|19|some.”||w15: The object “some” is supplied in English from context. εὑρήσετε supplies “you will find.”
john.21.7|27|himself—|w25|w31: The first “himself” reflects the middle verb διεζώσατο. ἑαυτόν is the object of the later “threw.”
